first_impression.reaction: Short intro, fine. It promises 15 styles but doesn't name a single one, and then the key takeaways are about maintenance and flying, not the styles. I searched 'engagement ring styles' and I still don't have the list. I kept going only because I could see numbered headings below.

journey.quote: Below, 15 engagement ring styles face the same four questions: does it match the wearer's personality, does it survive their everyday life, how does it sit on their hand, and how does it travel and photograph at a wedding abroad.
journey.reaction: OK, 15, good. But just name them here. Also, a wedding abroad? I'm looking at rings on the train, not planning a destination wedding.

journey.quote: Fly with the ring in your carry-on, tell your insurer your travel dates and confirm the policy covers loss and damage as well as theft.
journey.reaction: This is a key takeaway for a styles search? Feels off-topic. I wanted 'the main styles are X, Y, Z' up here.

journey.quote: When you don't know the wearer's hand well, a round or princess centre or a three-stone layout is the safest choice, as GIA says these suit almost any finger.
journey.reaction: This one is actually useful, and GIA as the source makes me trust it.

journey.quote: **Think twice if:** they work with their hands or snorkel often.
journey.reaction: The 'suits you if / think twice if' format is great on a phone. I read the halo section because that's what I like, and it was quick and honest.

journey.section: Quick comparison: all 15 styles at a glance
journey.quote: ## Quick comparison: all 15 styles at a glance
journey.reaction: This table is exactly what I wanted. Why is it after all 15 sections? I'd have bookmarked the page from the top if this was there.

journey.quote: The main styles are solitaire, halo, hidden halo, three-stone, toi et moi, east-west, cluster, vintage-inspired, art deco, pavé, bezel style, split shank, eternity-style, bypass and coloured gemstone centres.
journey.reaction: There it is, the actual answer to my search, right at the very bottom. This line belongs in the first 100 words.

journey.quote: The question of spend is separate, and we cover it in our guide to [how much to spend on an engagement ring](/expert-advice/how-much-should-you-spend-on-an-engagement-ring).
journey.reaction: Good, that's my next question. I'd tap it.

unanswered_questions: When was this written or updated? Is this still current for 2026?
Which of these styles cost more or less? Even a rough 'halo and pavé cost more than a plain solitaire' would help.
Which styles are popular right now versus classic?

turn_offs_found.quote: Choose the overall style first and the setting that holds the stone second, because GIA treats them as two separate decisions.
turn_offs_found.why: The answer to my actual question (the list of styles) is buried in the FAQ and a table near the end. The takeaways answer questions I didn't ask.

turn_offs_found.quote: **On the trip:** book a check before you fly, not after.
turn_offs_found.why: Every one of the 15 styles has an 'On the trip' line. Fine once, but 15 times it feels like the page is about destination weddings, not rings. Plus 15 ring photos down the page is a lot of scrolling on mobile.

would_share_with: My boyfriend, with the comparison table screenshotted
A friend who just got engaged and is choosing a style

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [talk to Wedded Concierge about a wedding abroad](/wonderland-concierge).
cta_reaction.why: I'm not even engaged yet. A wedding abroad planning service is way down the track. I'd click the spend guide or the trends link, not this.

top_3_changes: Name all 15 styles in the intro or the first key takeaway (the FAQ line 'The main styles are solitaire, halo...' basically does it), so the search answer is in the first 100 words.
Move the 'Quick comparison: all 15 styles at a glance' table up, straight after the key takeaways, so I can scan and bookmark.
Swap the carry-on/insurance key takeaway for a style-focused one, and add a 'last updated' date.
